Fresco: business feature map

What Fresco does for its users, feature by feature: the catalogue by module, who can create, read, update or delete what, the routes and screens behind it, and what could not be verified.

overview · module-auth-guest · module-onboarding · module-menu-generation · module-calendar · module-shopping-list · module-learning-loop · module-recipes · module-favorites · module-profile · module-billing · module-notices-push · module-motion · module-consent-legal · module-security · module-public-site · module-app-shell · module-food-safety · module-admin · module-observability · module-ops-tooling · module-supermarket · module-substitution · module-menu-history · crud-matrix · route-inventory · ui-inventory · integrations · flags-and-wip · discovery-gaps

Overview

Scope: full system. This is the feature-centric map of Fresco, a weekly menu planner for Spanish households whose menus learn from what each Pro household cooks and discards. It says what a user (or a job) can DO, grouped by module: the feature catalogue, the CRUD matrix, the routes behind the features, the UI inventory, integrations, flags and the gaps. Entities, access control, triggers and state machines are in the data map (bun run context:map business-data-context); route contracts and the auth model are in the API map (bun run context:map business-api-context). This map cites them and does not restate them.

Sources read: the page tree under app/ (pages and app/api/ route handlers), proxy.ts, components/, lib/, the nine Edge Functions in supabase/functions/ (Supabase-direct calls from lib/api/ count as features), the migration files in supabase/migrations/ (schema source is migrations per stack.database.schema_source, read offline), package.json, .github/workflows/, scripts/, .context/ADR/ (through ADR-0068), the last 30 commits plus the commits since 2026-10-14 and the companion data map (read 2026-10-29). The legacy markdown map .context/business/business-feature-map.md (last refreshed 2026-10-14) was read as INPUT (this section cites it in data-migrated-from) and was not deleted. Every row's evidence paths were re-checked against the tree and the rows touched since 2026-10-14 were re-read against code; discovery-gaps lists what was carried without a handler-level re-read.

Catalogue size: 658 active recipes (production read 2026-10-30, FRESCO-953). Every other live count (total recipes, seasonal ingredients, users, plans, Pro subscribers) is a database fact and is not hard-coded here: ask business-data-context (entity-recipes, entity-recipe-season, entity-user-profiles).

Not observed: the running app, the hosted database and the deployed Edge Function versions were not inspected for this map; .env.example could not be read in this session (permission denied), so the flag table is built from the environment variables the code reads. See discovery-gaps.

Inventory

139 catalogued features: 132 Stable, 3 Beta, 4 Planned, 0 WIP, 0 Deprecated. Status means: Stable shipped and reachable; Beta built but with part of its path not used by the product yet; Planned named in code, docs or ADRs with no working path. WIP is empty because no live unmerged feature work was found (see flags-and-wip).

Journeys that cross several features

  • Guest to paying Pro: FEAT-001 session, FEAT-014 wizard, FEAT-020 first menu, FEAT-119 push prompt, FEAT-077 keep-this-menu card, FEAT-126 then FEAT-003 conversion (FEAT-004 on an email conflict), FEAT-099 summary and FEAT-098 waiver, FEAT-059 Checkout, FEAT-060 webhook, FEAT-132 confirmation email.
  • Plan, shop, cook: FEAT-020 generation, FEAT-029 and FEAT-030 calendar, FEAT-115 add a recipe, FEAT-097 substitution, FEAT-033 list, FEAT-123 stale list refresh, FEAT-088 supermarket links, FEAT-032 marks.
  • Learning loop: FEAT-032 mark, FEAT-038 once-per-user count, FEAT-039 Pro read-back, FEAT-040 explanation, FEAT-127 Free preview (figure in module-learning-loop).
  • Account end of life: FEAT-057 export, FEAT-011 deletion with Stripe cancellation and refund, FEAT-112 PostHog erasure retry, FEAT-013 guest cleanup.
  • Catalogue safety: FEAT-079 filter, FEAT-120 tag barrier, FEAT-121 season barrier, FEAT-122 hosted audit, FEAT-082 admin delete.

Auth and guest mode

How a visitor becomes a user: a real anonymous session first, an account later without losing the menu. Authorization everywhere is row ownership through auth.uid(), never a role column (ADR-0003); the signed-in layout also sends a visitor with no session to /login.

Menu generation

The deterministic engine that fills a week of up to 21 slots (7 days by desayuno, comida, cena) from the catalogue after a SQL food-safety filter. No external LLM runs in production (ADR-0005).

FEAT-020: Weekly menu generation

IDFEAT-020
StatusStable
EndpointsPOST /generate-meal-plan (Edge Function)
UIPost-onboarding loading, then /menu and /calendar
OwnersGuest, Free, Pro
Dependenciesget_filtered_recipes(), menu-selector.ts, create_meal_plan(), user_profiles, recipes
Evidencesupabase/functions/generate-meal-plan/{index,menu-selector}.ts; ADR-0005
  • ✓ Implemented: Fills up to 21 slots with an in-process scored heuristic: category and richness variety against the previous slot, a season bonus for the planned week, a nudge from the recipe's global cook and discard counts, a seeded tie-break jitter
  • ✓ Implemented: Same user and same week give the same menu: the seed is user:semana_iso and the season comes from the planned week's Monday, not the clock (FRESCO-380, FRESCO-1012)
  • ✓ Implemented: The shopping budget is compared per person: each slot's cost bucket is scaled by the household size (FRESCO-1009)
  • ✓ Implemented: 409 when a plan already exists for the week; 422 when fewer than 21 safe recipes survive the filter
  • ✓ Implemented: A slot with no safe candidate gets the no-safe-recipe sentinel and a templated advertencias entry instead of a failure
  • ✓ Implemented: The plan and all its slots are written in ONE transaction by create_meal_plan() (service role only), so a timeout cannot leave a slot-less plan that answers 409 for ever; a user may hold at most 104 plans

Subscription and billing

Pro is sold through Stripe hosted Checkout. The Stripe webhook is the only real-time writer of subscription state on user_profiles, enforced by a database trigger (ADR-0007); the daily reconciliation is the second writer. Money-path code lives in lib/billing/.

Supermarket layer

Links and prices on shopping-list lines, one weekly cost figure, and an export. What a user sees today comes from committed generated catalogues read at render time; nothing on the request path calls a chain. A Postgres price model and its refresh runner exist but the app does not read them yet. Legal state is executable: every connector declares permiso and only concedido or riesgo-aceptado run (ADR-0027, ADR-0028, ADR-0036, ADR-0037).

Legend. A feature id means a screen, route or job performs it end to end. System-owned means a job, trigger, migration or the owner writes it and no user path exists. By design means the data model forbids it (append-only, toggle-only, cascade-only).

Discovery gaps

What could not be verified or looks unfinished. Each item says what to ask or grep next.

Not verified this pass

  1. Running app and hosted state. The app was not run, the hosted database was not queried and Edge Function or migration deployment state was not compared with the repo. Active recipes: 658 (production read 2026-10-30, FRESCO-953); every other live count is deliberately not stated. Ask or run: supabase migration list --linked and bun scripts/check-functions-drift.ts.
  2. .env.example unread. Reading it was denied in this session, so defaults and the full variable list come from process.env and Deno.env references only; the flag table may omit a documented variable.
  3. Behaviour carried from the legacy map. The rows' evidence paths were checked to exist and the rows touched by FRESCO-1000..1063 were re-read against code (marks, learning, shopping list, consents, waitlist, billing guards, season, tags, search, nav, offline, headers). Capability bullets of long-stable rows (for example FEAT-006, 008, 010, 031, 046..048, 051, 052, 066..069, 071, 077, 078, 085, 086) were not re-read handler by handler. Grep next: each row's Evidence column.
  4. Pro and Family usage. Whether any Pro subscriber exists in production was not re-read; the Pro branch of generation and the whole billing domain may still be unexercised against real subscription data. Ask: state-user-profiles and entity-user-profiles in the data map.
  5. PRD and SRS drift. Not re-read; the legacy map said they still described Gemini and a two-layer allergen guardrail (FRESCO-302).

Mismatches with the data map (not blocking)

  1. Catalogue creation has no feature. The data map's flow-catalog-curation writes recipes through service-role scripts and data migrations; the only in-product catalogue operation is delete (FEAT-082). Creating or editing a recipe has no UI and no Edge Function. Ask: where the generation tooling for the next catalogue batches lives (FRESCO-953 work).
  2. Supermarket tables are written and never read by a feature. The data map describes entity-supermarket-layer and a price runner; the feature map has FEAT-094 and FEAT-095 in Beta and FEAT-137 Planned. Ask: when FEAT-088 and FEAT-089 switch to get_supermarket_prices.
  3. Tables with no user-facing feature: recipe_user_feedback, ingredient_seasons, recipe_season_exceptions, billing_mode, rate_limit_endpoints, rate_limit_exempt_users (emptied) are system-owned and appear in the CRUD matrix as such.
  4. lib/supabase/types.ts is behind the migrations (data map): features that use create_meal_plan, the season tables or account_erasures rely on untyped calls until bun run db:types runs.

Behaviour gaps found in code

  1. No screen issues sustituida. update-recipe-status accepts it with a safety re-check and the trigger no-ops on it, but the calendar uses drag swap (FEAT-030) and per-ingredient substitution is a different mechanism (FEAT-097). Possibly dead or planned. Grep next: sustituida across components/ (only lib/api/open-slots.ts reads the state).
  2. Confirmation emails cannot reach real customers. Resend sends from onboarding@resend.dev, which delivers only to the account owner; FEAT-132 retries and reports to Sentry, FEAT-111 sends the waitlist confirmation through the same sender, and FEAT-136 is Planned behind the same missing domain (FRESCO-886). Ask: the date a domain is owned.
  3. The waitlist has no reader. Nothing in the repo exports, counts or mails the confirmed list (FEAT-111, FEAT-125). Ask: who runs the launch-day export.
  4. One Supabase project serves local, staging and production (.agents/project.yaml). The Stripe mode guard (FEAT-130) was built for it; every other write path is shared. Deliberate, but every gap compounds.
  5. Legal texts are provisional and the risk is accepted by the founder (ADR-0066); LEGAL_TEXTS_VERSION is provisional-*. Ask: the date a lawyer reviews them.
  6. Per-store pricing is a placeholder. Fresco stores no postcode; any per-store claim in copy would be unbacked (FEAT-088, 094).
  7. Rate-limit cleanup has no heartbeat (FEAT-110); a stopped cleanup raises no alert.
  8. Shopping-list refresh keeps comprado by name and unit; a renamed ingredient between two catalogue versions would come back unchecked. Read from merge-refresh.ts, not exercised.

Differences from the legacy markdown map (code wins)

  1. CSP is enforcing with a per-request nonce (proxy.ts, lib/security/csp.ts); the legacy map said Report-Only.
  2. Catalogue search ignores accents since FRESCO-1011; the legacy map listed that as a known gap.
  3. Learning counts once per user and recipe and the rating path is gone (FRESCO-1012, ADR-0063); marks are changeable inside the current week with a 10 s undo (FRESCO-1014).
  4. Five jobs are heartbeat-monitored, not one; generate-shopping-list and the export are rate limited; the sex field left the onboarding identity step (migration 20261019160000); onboarding consents are written by a server function (FRESCO-1007), not a client insert.
  5. Supermarket price age is shown and hidden past 30 days (FRESCO-1028), re-applied after a hold.
  6. Catalogue size moved with FRESCO-953; the legacy figures are not repeated (see overview).
